head: 1e58780fbfeaaec8f1bdde05120b5f3dacc8bae7
title: A covered repo passed in URL or other non-canonical form silently gets the platform PAT.
reason: The PR description says on purpose that "A URL, a third segment or a ./.. segment skips the provider tier", and resolve_github_token has no call site yet, so this is intended behaviour.

head: 1e58780fbfeaaec8f1bdde05120b5f3dacc8bae7
title: A wall-clock bound in a unit test can fail on a slow or loaded CI runner.
reason: The flakiness claim is a guess: about 16,000 × 512 single-class backtrack steps run in sre's fast repeat loop take tens of milliseconds, well under the 0.5 s bound, so no real failure is shown.

head: 06b90ae503e80213e8c3af657ed67c22f5312f03
title: The documented `rule_refused` remedy still says "share the agent", unlike the changed admin message.
reason: The row at approvals.md:189 is out of date, but it is documentation wording only; the actual rule_refused message changed and no behaviour goes wrong.

head: 06b90ae503e80213e8c3af657ed67c22f5312f03
title: The troubleshooting remedy for a held credential entry leaves out the blocked and deactivated causes.
reason: The remedy sentence in troubleshooting.md:205 is a doc wording remark, not a code defect.

head: 06b90ae503e80213e8c3af657ed67c22f5312f03
title: Public `reachable_people` was removed without a replacement under that name.
reason: A search for `reachable_people` finds it only in the security-report docs (one of which records its removal) and in no code, so no caller can raise AttributeError.

head: bb4c0e3ddba219c994fddf971198996b45819d79
title: A top-level `import psycopg` stops the whole test module loading under psycopg2.
reason: requirements.txt:37 pins psycopg[c]==3.3.6 and unittests/test_async_delete.py:20 already imports psycopg at module level, so psycopg 3 is the project's driver and a top-level import cannot fail on a supported setup.

head: 3e0d6cff2708c94a8440df4823469e1f53767cee
title: New refusal of a dimension role change is not part of #1507.
reason: Scope remark only; the discussion explicitly says the three review fixes (including DIMENSION_HAS_CODES for #1503) were added on top of this PR on purpose.

head: 3e0d6cff2708c94a8440df4823469e1f53767cee
title: A failing language list now fails the job, and the list may not be the provider's source languages.
reason: getAvailableLanguages returns feature.config.availableLanguages, documented in ai-feature.controller.js:56 as 'Available target languages', so a French email in an en/nl-only company (or one with an empty list, meaning all allowed) loses its fr source and falls back to guessing; a failing lookup also now fails the detectSourceLanguage step.

head: 3e0d6cff2708c94a8440df4823469e1f53767cee
title: Unrequested change to the published `locale` template value, which may leave `lang` stale.
reason: Scope is explained in the discussion (#1505 fix), and the loop at lines 43-45 sets values['locale'] = '' when the legacy locale dimension has no selection, so the value is not left missing.

head: 3c71fe893496207bb5dccc8ebf015c5f7ba0ae1f
title: An unset belief_time may stop the lookup from finding existing annotations, so repeat posts create duplicates.
reason: belief_time is `db.Column(..., nullable=True)` with no default (line 25), so an annotation without a belief time is stored as NULL, and `Annotation.belief_time == None` becomes `IS NULL` and matches that stored row.

head: 3c71fe893496207bb5dccc8ebf015c5f7ba0ae1f
title: `scalar_one_or_none()` can raise MultipleResultsFound on existing rows that match the new, wider key.
reason: The CLI creates annotations without a belief time (data_add.py 1029-1037, 1058-1060), PostgreSQL treats NULLs as distinct in annotation_content_key, and the old lookup included `end`, so rows differing only in end can exist; the new filter matches several of them and scalar_one_or_none() raises MultipleResultsFound.

head: 201c6dae4ca33fcafffe0cb02c793cb215a801e1
title: The new SDF_LZ4 branch takes over the return of the UE_IO branch, so IoStore jobs fall through.
reason: Patch lines 268-272 show the added `if ... == SDF_LZ4:` block inserted between `ue_io_shaders(...)` and the unchanged `return rel, uniq_keys(found), ...` line, so that return now belongs to the SDF branch and UE_IO jobs fall through to the rest of `scan_file_in`; the maintainer's review reports the same blocker.

head: 560786c37e3658457a0821b119d322bb767045bc
title: Battery level formula is not clamped to 0–100 %.
reason: The lambda filter in features/battery-voltage.yaml line 39 already clamps the level to 0–100 (`std::min(100.0f, std::max(0.0f, x))`) and leaves NAN as it is.

head: 92f784b94f218c58d45b481aba4a13723f51e298
title: Local `nativeThreadId` still holds the expired checkpoint's thread ID after it is dropped
reason: The local nativeThreadId is written back only in onAccepted (conversation.ts:1050), which runs from native.run at turn.ts:113, after onThread at turn.ts:107 has already replaced it; any failure before then throws out of execute, so the dead thread ID never reaches the record.

head: d8682e7a9af21ba8a4ff0946f3716ef442ccaea6
title: The usage insert takes the student only from the assessment instance, which can break group-assessment submissions.
reason: In shared-question-usages.sql, the participants CTE uses `coalesce(ai.user_id, tu.user_id)` with a LEFT JOIN on team_users, so team members are expanded, and line 58 filters `p.user_id IS NOT NULL`, so a NULL user_id can never reach the insert.

head: f82775f7eac6be8be96a0462803545b0a07bedf0
title: New automatic consent re-prompt for ordinary monitors
reason: The fresh-consent retry at lines 445-447 is a deliberate change in prompting, not a defect: it shows the host dialog when the saved consent restores the wrong monitor, which the existing error text ('choose this monitor in the host dialog') already expects; nothing breaks.

head: f82775f7eac6be8be96a0462803545b0a07bedf0
title: Every switched-away monitor is parked, not only the shadowed PBP half
reason: Pausing every monitor on switch-away is the stated design ('切出或驻留会话时' pause the stream), and end() at lines 400-406 closes every non-shadowed spare on disconnect, as the description promises.

head: f82775f7eac6be8be96a0462803545b0a07bedf0
title: Lead/shadowed choice follows Mutter's logical-monitor order, which may not match the portal's restore order
reason: Speculative and self-admittedly unchecked: uu_portal_monitors iterates Mutter's logical monitors from GetCurrentState, which (from memory, not verified in the repo) is the same list and order xdg-desktop-portal-gnome walks when restoring consent, and the author tested on real PBP hardware.

head: f82775f7eac6be8be96a0462803545b0a07bedf0
title: A portal desktop stream with no input owner yet exits without streaming or logging anything.
reason: role.input is set at webrtc.rs:295 ('if desktop { *role.input.lock().unwrap() = Some(input.desktop_session()); }'), before spawn at line 489, so the owner is Some for desktop connections.

head: f82775f7eac6be8be96a0462803545b0a07bedf0
title: If `switch_screen` returns `Ok(None)`, the request carries on as if no screen change was asked for.
reason: select_for sends Portal switches to switch_to, which returns Ok(()) at portal.rs:434 without calling publish when the session already captures the connector, so switched stays None and the request continues with no reject even though the selection never changed.

head: b112503b1761cd1b7f02697ab23ef66c2ca19a75
title: Per-line grid opacity checks both axis styles instead of the line's own axis.
reason: is_axis_style_entry accepts `Automatic` (graphics.rs:11842), so `{Automatic, Directive[Red]}` gives (None, Some); grid_alpha at plot.rs:6182-6185 checks both slots and is used for both axes, so a self-colored x line gets 1.0 instead of 0.4.

head: dad629b193271731674b6d20b14ff23e5bf52bb8
title: `task_statuses` skips every task after a build that returned composition errors.
reason: When composition_errors is non-empty the function returns Err(RoverClientError::SubgraphBuildErrors{subgraph, graph_ref, source}) at lines 211-227, so task_summaries is never put into a CheckWorkflowResponse and no truncated data.task_statuses can be emitted.

head: b360ab9fd75765c7eac39d1be378a833ca8544ff
title: Quick toggles start helper runs that can finish in either order, so the panel can end up in the opposite state from the switch.
reason: glue.rs:404-412 starts a separate pkexec run on every toggle with nothing ordering them, `panel_refresh_set` only acts on Err, and `helper::write` (panel_refresh.rs:188) uses one shared `path.with_extension("new")` temp file, so quick on/off toggles can leave the panel and the saved choice opposite to the menu, or fail on the rename.

head: b360ab9fd75765c7eac39d1be378a833ca8544ff
title: At boot, `apply` stops waiting if Intel's driver hasn't bound yet, so PSR stays at the kernel default (on) and the switch is hidden.
reason: module.nix orders the unit only after `sys-kernel-debug.mount`, and the wait loop in aizome-panel-refresh.rs breaks as soon as `!intel_display()`, which only checks for a bound xe/i915 driver under /sys/class/drm; if the module hasn't bound yet, `run` writes `available=false` and leaves PSR at the driver default (on).

head: f20ab5e83d94a55f133293cfa8f8e58de07cde65
title: Arrow UTF-8 bytes are checked against the database encoding, not decoded from UTF-8.
reason: The missing UTF-8-to-server conversion was already there before this PR: before it, an EUC_JP database stored UTF-8 bytes that are invalid in that encoding, which is the corruption this PR stops. The check deliberately copies pq_text_cell_ok, and the reviewer already flagged the conversion as a non-blocking follow-up shared with the Parquet reader ('not a regression').

head: 2666b3b115fb46f49408349fd4d101a2aea1856a
title: Quickstart code still asks for the removed 'Everett Mono' font.
reason: Searching ui/ turns up 'Everett' only in these inline fontFamily stacks and no @font-face for it, so with the Everett files deleted these snippets fall back to the browser's default monospace.

head: 2666b3b115fb46f49408349fd4d101a2aea1856a
title: Three provider brand colors were changed even though the PR says provider colors are left alone.
reason: Remark only: the openai and bedrock fills are the same dark green and amber tones as before, so nothing breaks; the finding is really that the change differs from the description.

head: 2666b3b115fb46f49408349fd4d101a2aea1856a
title: Unguarded decodeURIComponent can crash the whole app shell.
reason: breadcrumbsFor line 104 calls decodeURIComponent without a guard, but whether Next.js routing rejects malformed percent-escapes before usePathname hands them to this code can't be checked in the repo.

head: 2666b3b115fb46f49408349fd4d101a2aea1856a
title: StatusBadge builds `badge-${tone}` class names that may not exist for every tone, such as `badge-yellow`.
reason: globals.css defines .badge-yellow at line 321, along with .badge-green, .badge-red and .badge-neutral.

head: 2666b3b115fb46f49408349fd4d101a2aea1856a
title: Disabled styling may be lost when the buttons switch to `.btn` classes.
reason: globals.css line 189 defines .btn:disabled with opacity 0.5 and cursor not-allowed.

head: 2666b3b115fb46f49408349fd4d101a2aea1856a
title: Save button loses its disabled styling and size class.
reason: globals.css gives .btn a default 28px height with 0 8px padding and styles .btn:disabled (lines 166-192), so the button still has padding and dims while saving.

head: bf16d5561ed62aceac55e9fd81976fd491459ffa
title: Coroutines created in Lua inherit the count hook and keep one budget across all later calls.
reason: getLuaState() (environment.cpp:247-254) opens only the base, table, string and math libraries, never luaopen_coroutine, so scripts cannot call coroutine.create/wrap; the only lua_newthread in src (callback.h:66) already clears the inherited hook.

head: a2669342ca17bf49ec71236f8f17750b511f9da4
title: Unrequested change to which secret the Studio CI job uses for credentials.
reason: The secret change has its own commit ('ci(studio): use STUDIO_READ_ACCESS_TOKEN in tests-studio.yml') and falls back to the old secret, so this is a remark about scope rather than a defect.

head: a2669342ca17bf49ec71236f8f17750b511f9da4
title: update_dataset_version now writes created_at for every caller, not just touch_reservation.
reason: No caller passes created_at: catalog.py:1109's **values holds only stats and preview fields, and a search of src/ finds no created_at= passed to update_dataset_version except touch_reservation.

head: a2669342ca17bf49ec71236f8f17750b511f9da4
title: New writer branch in insert_stored_rows is unused by the listing writer and changes shared behaviour.
reason: insert_block's contract says rows 'carry their sys__id', so sending callers that omit sys__id (e.g. records.py:141) to the writer, which assigns ids, is deliberate; the finding only objects that the change is unexplained.

head: 362c4ccfe64f7d0f590272ac9791a99db2fbe254
title: The version `sources` field is reused to store a version string, then parsed as a semver.
reason: In this repo a listing version's `sources` is only ever the default "" (create_dataset/create_dataset_version default sources="", and the only real `sources=` writer is the non-listing `create_dataset_from_sources` at catalog.py:1584) or the version string written at listing.py:653, so `semver.value(prev_ver.sources)` at line 633 never sees a non-version string.

head: 6bc9e60c407b209d3ef8ea5dfa60ae40bbafd7df
title: Agg no longer gets the rows of each partition in the user's order.
reason: The agg input query keeps the user's ORDER BY through the join, and the old Partition sorted by `partition_col, *query._order_by_clauses`; dataset_select_paginated (warehouse.py:180) now does `.order_by(None).order_by(*keys)` with only (partition_id, sys__id), so rows inside a partition arrive in sys__id order instead of the user's order.

head: 6bc9e60c407b209d3ef8ea5dfa60ae40bbafd7df
title: `Partition` no longer sorts its query by partition, so it now relies on whatever `execute` does.
reason: Both callers (dataset.py:802 and dispatch.py:81) pass dataset_select_paginated, which always sorts by partition_id first when the query is partitioned (warehouse.py:171-180); the unsorted override the finding imagines does not exist in the repo.

head: 52e6865e8c440b5d60b8f638ddf519d69971a1c5
title: `self.url()` can cost an extra Hub request on every read that goes to the Hub.
reason: PinnedHfFileSystem overrides url() (hf_file_system.py:187-197) to build the URL with hf_hub_url from resolve_path without calling isdir/info, so self.url() on line 84 makes no extra paths_info request.

head: 56e43481860ad807307b9c4672e942b79723693c
title: Adds a required native dependency and a subprocess SQLite writer that the column-projection request doesn't cover.
reason: This is a scope remark, not a defect: the commit list includes the stacked base a60df5a (#2223, native Arrow ingestion), which explains the ADBC dependency and writer, and the description says the PR is stacked.

head: 56e43481860ad807307b9c4672e942b79723693c
title: `save()` now renames the UDF output table straight into the dataset, which goes beyond column projection.
reason: This is also a scope remark about the save() rename path, which comes from the stacked Arrow-ingestion work; it names no concrete failure.

head: 56e43481860ad807307b9c4672e942b79723693c
title: Every `apply_steps` now imports pyarrow, even for chains with no Arrow reader.
reason: src/datachain/lib/arrow.py imports only stdlib modules and numpy at module level, not pyarrow, so the claim that it loads pyarrow and turns on the per-row RecordBatch checks is false.

head: 56e43481860ad807307b9c4672e942b79723693c
title: The Arrow fast path picks an arbitrary type from `kept`, which can disagree with the row path.
reason: value_codec in codec.py:563-565 always builds `kept` with exactly one type (frozenset({str}) or frozenset({py_type})), so next(iter(codec.kept)) is never an arbitrary pick.

head: 56e43481860ad807307b9c4672e942b79723693c
title: The child's stderr is piped but only read after the child dies, so a chatty child can deadlock the load.
reason: The child _run catches adbc errors and reports them as JSON on stdout, and nothing in it writes to stderr per batch, so the >64 KB stderr output the finding needs is speculative.

head: 3a540fbf908c7c1b7ea824d25039200485247781
title: Changing the default delta key on GCS can break delta pipelines saved before this change
reason: The "change delta key" error in delta.py:80-86 is raised only when a chain step (mutate/select/gen) rewrites a key column, as the tests at test_delta.py:1213-1255 show; delta does not store the previous run's key or compare it with the new one. The new key (file.path, file.version) uses columns that the old result rows already have, so upgraded pipelines still match their earlier results.

head: 1ac4256d36330b7ba5ee9b29d9f3c8ab42ddfa3e
title: The joined title folder name no longer has any length limit.
reason: Line 45 joins titles that were each cut by `slugify` with `--`, and nothing cuts the result again, so two 150-byte titles or several 64-character titles make a folder name over the 255-byte limit.

head: 1ac4256d36330b7ba5ee9b29d9f3c8ab42ddfa3e
title: Slugifying test file paths lets different spec files share one step folder.
reason: run-step.ts:105 checks only `header.test !== scope.testTitle` and never the test file, while line 44 now lowercases and slugifies file segments, so `sign up.spec.ts` and `sign-up.spec.ts` share a key without any error.

head: 7bb007aecd91f0f859d1612b214123bdc427610f
title: Bump to diadata v1.4.714 may point at a release that doesn't exist yet or lacks a go.sum entry.
reason: The discussion says 'PR Validation creates the v1.4.714 release' and #1309 did the same, so this is the intended process. The restServer go.sum has no diadata entry even for v1.4.712, so the bump adds no new go.sum problem.

head: d6ac5fa3ede487e0ba6c5e86fb55ce6e8e72cea9
title: Concurrent PUTs to the same key can share a temp file name.
reason: Line 22 names the temp file `${file}.${process.pid}.${Date.now()}.tmp`, so two PUTs to the same key in the same millisecond on one server share a path; they can interleave writes, and the second fs.rename fails with ENOENT, which becomes a 500. The trigger is narrow but real, and nothing serializes the writes.

head: b7b435eb2124bf140b33e3bddae3025a235240ba
title: The linking -en- rule also removes final stress from Latinate -endeer/-enseer verbs.
reason: `@CenL20) ee (r_` at nl_rules:301 matches agendeer (a-g-en-d-ee-r) and recenseer (e-c-en-s-ee-r), since L20 includes d and s. These verbs then get unstressed `I`, and no nl_list entry or test exempts them.

head: b7b435eb2124bf140b33e3bddae3025a235240ba
title: `model` has no guard for `modellen`/`modelleren`, unlike `hotel`, `tabel` and `snel`.
reason: Only `model (C@P5` and `model (l@P5` exist (nl_rules:861-862), with no `(le` guard like hotel/tabel/snel. So modellen and modelleren are split as compounds, and no list entry covers them.

head: b7b435eb2124bf140b33e3bddae3025a235240ba
title: Common adjectives derived from compounds now get first-element stress (oorspronkelijk, huishoudelijk).
reason: oorspronkelijk/oorzakelijk match `oor (C@P3` (line 969), huishoudelijk matches `huis (C@P4` (line 602) and spreekwoordelijk matches `spreek (C@P6`. None is in nl_list, unlike hoofdzakelijk, so all get first-element stress.

head: 9d387ace23e145ab0d210aee5e8ac31295c4dc4d
title: Integrated devices without an energy collector now always report 0 charged energy.
reason: configureChargerType (loadpoint.go:508-511) always creates a charge meter, so a missing collector is the only way to skip wiring; per the discussion that only happens for the config UI instance, which never runs, and the fallback was removed on purpose in e75c9009f.

head: 9d387ace23e145ab0d210aee5e8ac31295c4dc4d
title: The translation key `main.loadpoint.todayEnergy` may not exist.
reason: i18n/en.json:1707 defines "todayEnergy": "Today", and Loadpoint.vue:80 already uses main.loadpoint.todayEnergy.

head: 062992661ca19a00e624c37d36c2329221ac207d
title: Room refresh failures are dropped with no log and no signal to peers.
reason: refreshOnce (hub.go:630-648) discards both the FetchChanges error and the Apply error without logging them. FetchChanges in persist.go:409-456 only wraps and returns its errors, and hub.go has no logger. A persistent failure (heads that cannot be decoded, a snapshot that will not load, ErrRefreshIncomplete) therefore goes unseen, and the reset to a zero position makes every 500 ms poll rebuild fro

head: 3d9aa25dc2adcad26de3112d48dc8eeea49802cb
title: Ensure moves the source to whichever account was noted last, so deleting that account orphans the source.
reason: Ensure's ON CONFLICT (lines 94-98) always overwrites connector_account_id with the most recently noted account. connector_accounts is only unique per (connector_id, external_account_id), so two connectors in one org can share an external ID. Deleting the last-noted one sets the link to NULL and LoadNextDueForUpdateSkipLocked skips the source while the other account is still live.

head: 3d9aa25dc2adcad26de3112d48dc8eeea49802cb
title: cloudfront is imported directly but listed as `// indirect`.
reason: The `// indirect` marker on the cloudfront line in go.mod is bookkeeping that `go mod tidy` fixes, not a code defect.

head: 3d9aa25dc2adcad26de3112d48dc8eeea49802cb
title: Backfill links and schedules every AWS connector account, including disabled ones.
reason: ConnectorAccount has no enabled/status column, and DisableAccount calls account.Delete, so every connector_accounts row the backfill reads is a live account.

head: df7f8a828ebb1a2da03fc86c570ad4bbffa53798
title: Signed 32-bit mul_shift_right with q > 32 may still fall back to a 64-bit multiply.
reason: In src/FindIntrinsics.cpp lines 1563-1568, lower_mul_shift_right rewrites q > bits as mul_shift_right(a, b, a.type().bits()) followed by >> (q - bits), so signed int32 with q > 32 becomes a q == 32 call that the new branch catches; full_q = 31 is only used for q < full_q.

head: c196d53b7f6d604bb88d4e17f0fbffd7e0de1ce6
title: AccentVars switch the focus outline, expand icon, filter focus border and selection fill to --primary, which the PR says it does not change.
reason: Commit c196d53 deliberately adds AccentVars to follow --primary (with a test). The finding only points out that the PR description is out of date, which is a remark, not a defect.

head: c196d53b7f6d604bb88d4e17f0fbffd7e0de1ce6
title: Inlining default-theme values breaks user overrides of the variables they referenced.
reason: theme-default.css.ts declares the default variables on :root, so `--infinite-cell-border` and the other derived values were already resolved there. Setting `--infinite-cell-border-color` on the shadcn grid never changed them. Keeping the references, as suggested, would resolve them against the shadcn values (such as `Cell.borderWidth: '0px'`) and change the light colours.

head: d49c98bc271cb1a94e8e138057252ef0c09513c8
title: Extensionless documents with a dot in the name are now skipped silently.
reason: Line 348 checks `filepath.Ext(found) != ""`, and `filepath.Ext` returns the text after the last dot, so a Markdown file with no extension but a dot in its name (e.g. `release-1.2` → `.2`) fails `IsMarkdownFile` and is now skipped without a lookup or a `--check-links` report; before this change it was resolved, which breaks the PR's promise that extensionless files behave as before.

head: 22a6bf6bca3577835e0f0ba6129a683a6ff56612
title: Clearing the current repo before startup empties the repo list, so Desktop opens the demo graph instead of the user's other graphs.
reason: `repo-handler/get-repos` uses `db-persist/get-all-graphs`, which adds the `ipc "getGraphs"` disk graphs to the `<list-db` result (persist.cljs:33-40), so `repos` still lists the other graphs on disk.

head: 22a6bf6bca3577835e0f0ba6129a683a6ff56612
title: The current repo is compared to raw `getGraphs` names, which may not use the same format.
reason: Electron `getGraphs` returns `get-db-based-graphs`, documented as "Returns canonical DB graph repo names" and run through `canonicalize-db-version-repo`, so the names carry the `logseq_db_` prefix and match the repo URL form.

head: 22a6bf6bca3577835e0f0ba6129a683a6ff56612
title: `restore-and-setup!` now rethrows graph-absent errors, which can break callers other than startup.
reason: A search for `restore-and-setup!` finds only `<restore-or-demo!` and `<open-startup-repo!` (plus tests), and both catch the graph-absent rejection, so no other caller exists.

head: 377bea9de162116a94dda6948e872e3130682304
title: Rollback now reverses user txs while later :fix txs on the same entities stay applied, so the reversal can be left half done.
reason: Reversing an insert does not leave an orphan: reverse-tx-data (apply_txs.cljs:119-127) uses replace-attr-retract-with-retract-entity-v2, which turns the :block/uuid retract into [:db/retractEntity e] (normalize.cljs:31-32) and deletes the whole block including the :fix-set order; for moves, re-adding the old cardinality-one :block/order replaces Y, so the claimed half-done reversal does not happen

head: e3b1d6c78b46026415423cc76ad5abc3d73a5ce4
title: `droppedAsEmpty` may be left unused after removing the lookahead, which would break the build.
reason: `droppedAsEmpty` is still called at responses.go:6274 (`... || droppedAsEmpty(&m)`), so it is not unused and the build does not break.

head: e488295eea0120f6a2c50db1d88be7ec59a8a70b
title: Reads after cleanup() now fail with ErrStreamClosed instead of reaching the upstream.
reason: No caller reads after cleanup: every caller defers stopIdleTimeout(), largeresponse.go calls it after ReadAll, on errors or from LargeResponseReader cleanup, and relay/stream.go:284 calls s.stop() inside complete(), which runs only at end of stream or on Close.

head: e488295eea0120f6a2c50db1d88be7ec59a8a70b
title: Each zero-byte Read now restarts the idle deadline, so a stream that keeps returning (0, nil) never times out.
reason: Only time spent inside a pending Read counts, by design (the test was renamed to ZeroByteReadThenStallTimesOut), and the endless (0, nil) loop needs a wrapped fasthttp, net/http or gzip body reader to misbehave that way, which a remote server cannot cause.

head: 9a8525417cb6d3f660a98e5080864a1eb8320fac
title: Test reads the port and makes the login call in one return statement, but Go does not fix their order.
reason: Line 636 `return gotPort, runner.authLogin(...)` reads `gotPort`, which the OpenBrowser closure sets inside authLogin; the Go spec fixes the order only among calls, so the test's success depends on how the compiler orders the read.

head: 52bdad9bd327be821456a2af43d67e96baf24a3e
title: A retried save after a partial failure loses the fact that the router was turned on.
reason: withSavedRouting (routerSheet.utils.ts:97) puts `enabled` into the baseline once the routing PUT succeeds. On a retry after the name PUT fails, routerSheetChanges (line 69) leaves `enabled` out, so line 146 computes turnedOn=false: the user gets the plain "Router saved" toast and onSaved does not switch to the overview, even though this sheet turned the router on.

head: c1709d7d5c572c6ea2d55f13c10002a81446fab0
title: The shared mint limit lets anyone lock a chosen IP, or a whole site, out of login.
reason: get_the_user_ip() trusts the X-Forwarded-For header by default (functions.php:3985-3991), and the bucket is shared with the anonymous REST endpoint, so ~30 forged requests make login_CAPTCHA() print only an error (lines 3718-3720) and CAPTCHA_CHECK() reject the admin's login (line 3755); the author named the spoofing bypass but not this targeted lockout.

head: c1709d7d5c572c6ea2d55f13c10002a81446fab0
title: Errors the user can act on are now replaced with a generic "try again" message.
reason: PR description item 8 says all WP_Error branches, including core errors that carry data, now deliberately return the generic message, so this is an intended trade-off the author already stated.

head: 9cefcf0a973941e775f1d9fc62dc303f1ffe8d00
title: Focus-return change not covered by the PR description.
reason: The author explained this in the discussion: the focus-manager change fixes the MenuRoot.triggerless failure that the new unmount order causes, so the new layout needs it and the existing test covers it; the rest is about the PR description's wording.

head: 591d42add1773b5667e9db8e19f3e75954767fa3
title: `/ci` runs fork pull-request code with a `contents: write` token.
reason: pkgdown.yaml lines 34-38 and 53-55: a job with contents: write and GITHUB_PAT=secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN checks out refs/pull/N/merge on issue_comment and builds the PR's R package, so code from the PR runs with a write token.

head: 591d42add1773b5667e9db8e19f3e75954767fa3
title: Unrelated CI trigger rewrite stops pull requests from being checked on push.
reason: Deliberate policy change: the commit 'ci: run PR checks only on an approving review saying ready to be merged' and the workflow comment at lines 9-10 make it intentional; going beyond the PR description is a remark.

head: 591d42add1773b5667e9db8e19f3e75954767fa3
title: The approval gate does not check who reviewed the PR.
reason: Before this change the pull_request trigger ran CI for any PR author, and pull_request_review runs get a read-only token, so an unprivileged approver can start no more than anyone already could.

head: 591d42add1773b5667e9db8e19f3e75954767fa3
title: The status is reported on a head SHA that may not be the code that was tested.
reason: Line 73 stores head.sha from an API call made before the checkout of refs/pull/N/merge at line 88; a push in between makes the status at line 125 report a result for code that was not tested.

head: 591d42add1773b5667e9db8e19f3e75954767fa3
title: `startsWith(body, '/ci')` also matches other comments.
reason: startsWith(github.event.comment.body, '/ci') at line 31 also matches comments like '/cite', and unlike the review path the /ci path does not check the base ref, so stacked PRs run despite the header comment.

head: 2effbabbe3f229419378684ac394ca0f77d9daae
title: Right-clicking a state while its menu is open moves the time cursor instead of opening the menu again.
reason: Line 422 sets interact_pos to None while a PhaseMenuTarget is stored, so hovered_phase is None and a second right-click on a state removes the target and moves the cursor through clicked_time instead of reopening the menu.

head: 2effbabbe3f229419378684ac394ca0f77d9daae
title: "Jump to start of state" goes through `f64`, so large timestamps lose precision.
reason: Line 985 converts with `start_time as f64`, which is off by up to about 128 ns for nanosecond timestamps, while time_real.rs:92 already provides an exact `impl From<i64> for TimeReal`.

head: 3e29ad7128ee3b845fd40213756fe109628abf9f
title: A queued card arriving at a full live store is dropped from persistence straight away.
reason: Service.qml:181 `reserveLive` turns away any new key once `liveCount() >= maxLiveNotifications` (100, the same as LIVE_LIMIT), so a new queued card can never arrive while 100 rows are already live, and the trim at Store.js:217 never cuts a queued row that was just accepted.

head: 47d3b1abd28f6755979c52396960cac45e77cb92
title: Partition shutdown is turned into a generic storage error.
reason: Mapping the closed-admission error to `StorageError::OperationalError` (line 86) follows the same `.map_err(|_| StorageError::OperationalError)` convention used for gate and closure failures across partition-store. `from_journal_reader` (error.rs:258) only turns it into an ordinary JournalReader error, which is not retried in a way that matters while the partition is being torn down. head: 28328dfa73ee2360ed587c64f6756d5dc590223e
title: ForType leaks the pairing it built when it then throws ArgumentException.
reason: Release() (FindingDiffAnyTypePairing.cs:308) only calls Side.Complete(), which clears managed lists and calls SymbolKeyBuilder.Release() (`Reset(); _scratch = [];`). No pooled or unmanaged resource is involved, so the garbage collector frees an unreachable half-built pairing and nothing leaks.

head: 9bdc5f1c645e87ec01540cf90f9808663e883c12
title: Expulsion warning text colour is still hard-coded to white.
reason: Line 12 of penalty-list/index.css still sets `color: #fff` while its background is the themeable `var(--warn-3-bg)`, and common.css defines no variable for this text colour, so themes cannot change it as the PR intends.

head: f813c963b10fc9796fe585780a90d291cba7c35c
title: Merged initialState is a new object on every render, so Renderer may apply the saved filters again over the user's choice.
reason: useOpenUIState.ts:164-165 re-initializes only when the JSON of stateDeclarations and initialState changes, so a new object with the same content does nothing.

head: f813c963b10fc9796fe585780a90d291cba7c35c
title: The restored state is checked against the version only once and is still passed after the version on screen changes.
reason: restoredRef is reset only on [reads, id] (useLastResults.ts:275), so the v1 savedState is still passed after a new version arrives. useOpenUIState.ts:164-181 re-initializes with that initialState whenever the new version's stateDeclarations differ, which applies the stale v1 state to v2.

head: 5e7f5f9b138c5afbbc164cfbb58b5deebf84283f
title: Ported total goes up by two though only one game was added.
reason: The checklist entries at head run from line 11 to line 114, which is 104 games, so `44 / 104` is right; the author also said in the discussion that upstream's 102 was one short.

head: 5e7f5f9b138c5afbbc164cfbb58b5deebf84283f
title: Every vertex shader is paired with the same pixel shader, c1a608e6add64c26.
reason: This pairing is on purpose: `separable_pairs` in shader_split.py:1340-1351 pairs every single-stage vertex shader with a 'cover', the fewest pixel shaders whose inputs include those of all the others. When one pixel shader covers them all, every vertex shader gets the same one, and `vs_pad` only uses the union of the input locations.

head: 8be082fbfeccf42c67a9414c7d628b0d3576d2e9
title: A refreshing compact Kpi tile now only anchors the shimmer if the sheen is a direct child of the tile.
reason: CompactKpi.tsx line 30 puts <StateFrame compact> directly inside the .openui-dashboard-kpi-compact section, and StateFrame's refreshing branch (States.tsx 224-257) returns a fragment, so <Sheen/> is a direct child of the tile and the `:has(> .openui-dashboard-sheen)` rule matches; the data-compact rules only style the non-data states, which still get the wrapper.

head: 7408bb3f2750867b003e15fba47eef3e528a5571
title: Leftover inert-statement records from a failed load or non-file compile get reported against a later, unrelated load.
reason: `report_inert_statements` runs only after `setup_call_cleanup` in `load_metta_file_impl` returns normally, and it is the only code that retracts `inert_statement/2`. So records from a load that threw, or from `process_metta_string` and eval compiles, stay behind and are reported (or thrown under `--strict`) by the next outermost file load.

head: 7408bb3f2750867b003e15fba47eef3e528a5571
title: `data` erasure lives only in constrain_args, so clauses compiled with ConstrainArgs=false keep the literal `(data ...)` head.
reason: `ho_specialization(_, F)` holds only for specialized names. Their `translated_from` Input is built from `fun_meta(Args1, ...)` (specializer.pl:55-56), and `Args1` is the head after `constrain_args` has already removed `data`, so the ConstrainArgs=false path never sees a literal `(data ...)` head.

head: e958f3680edf514cba8c45cce441f6a78cf72c8c
title: Action samples likely won't compile in a project with ImplicitUsings turned on.
reason: Line 47's comment admits that `using System;` makes `Action<>` ambiguous, and the SDK adds `global using System;` when implicit usings are on (to my knowledge the Umbraco project template turns them on, though nothing in the repository shows it), so `: Action<ActionResult>` at line 26 and the `SendPeopleAction` base type at line 138 would fail with CS0104.
